title: Restructure variant maps and layer anchoring for Figma publish stability
creator: Elena Morales
description: Problem: We have growing publish failures, accidental instance breakage, and inconsistent runtime behavior caused by inconsistent variant organization, mixed layer anchoring patterns, and ambiguous naming conventions across buttons, tables and chart primitives. Goal: Produce a deterministic 'variant map' and a canonical set of layer-anchoring patterns (anchor, fixed, stretch) so teams can publish without regressions. Scope: - Audit existing button/table/chart components across primary library pages - Define canonical auto-layout axis and padding heuristics for small/medium/large density tokens - Create a migration script/checklist for renaming tokens and flattening accidental nested groups - Update Figma library with guarded publish steps (pre-publish linter, QA rubric, backout plan) Out of scope: building new components or changing visual language beyond mechanical restructuring.
acceptance_criteria: A documented variant map that lists canonical variant keys and allowed value sets for all button/table/chart families (stored in Design Confluence and linked in the ticket)
All components in the primary library follow the layer-anchoring pattern doc (anchor, fixed, stretch) and pass the pre-publish linter without warnings
Automatic Create/Update migration checklist and a small set of helper Figma plugins snippets to re-anchor misaligned layers
Published library with versioned tag (design-2026.03) and rollback instructions; no regressions reported by Solutions team during a 48-hour smoke window
At least two cross-functional reviewers (Engineering + PM) have signed off on the publish QA checklist
